title: Certificate Servicing Instruction: Carrying a Certificate of Deposit Into a New Term
content:
A term that has reached the end of its grace window without the owner closing the certificate is carried into a new term whatever the day the bank comes to record it, and the new term's figures are those of the day it is recorded.

## 1. What this governs

This instruction governs certificates of the Certificates of Deposit line. What it settles is the rate and the annual percentage yield the new term carries, together with the tier the certificate runs in, the first and last day of the new term, and the two markers showing which bonuses that rate includes. Nothing is paid out and the principal on the certificate is untouched.

The delay between the end of the grace window and the day the bank records the matter does not put the renewal out of reach; it is recorded when it is taken up.

## 2. Recording the renewal

The action is carried out with the agent-side tool `record_term_renewal_3666596b`, which is unlocked and then called by the agent. It writes the certificate as a certificate that is running again: its status becomes active, it is placed in the term tier given, the dates and the figures of the new term are written onto it, the one rate increase the term allows is made available again, and the count of terms the certificate has run through is raised by one.

## 3. The values the call takes

| Parameter | What it is |
|---|---|
| `certificate_id` | the reference number of the certificate being carried into a new term, as returned by the certificate lookup for this customer |
| `new_variant_name` | the official term tier the certificate runs in for the new term, spelled exactly |
| `new_term_start_date` | the first day of the new term, written as YYYY-MM-DD in the bank's local calendar with no time part |
| `new_maturity_date` | the last day of the new term, in the same date form |
| `new_interest_rate` | the annual interest rate the new term pays, as percent to 2 decimal places, for example 3.97, passed as a number and not as a string, already rounded to those two places |
| `new_apy` | the annual percentage yield the new term shows, as percent to 2 decimal places, for example 4.05, passed as a number, already rounded to those two places |
| `jumbo_bonus_applied` | whether the rate written for the new term includes the jumbo bonus: true where the rate carries jumbo bonus points of any size, false where it carries none at all |
| `relationship_bonus_applied` | whether the rate written for the new term includes the relationship bonus: true where the rate carries relationship bonus points of any size, false where it carries none at all |

The value of `new_variant_name` is one of six. **6-Month Certificate** applies where the new term is the bank's six month term; **11-Month No-Penalty Certificate**, the eleven month term that charges no penalty after its opening days; **12-Month Certificate**, the one year term; **18-Month Bump-Up Certificate**, the eighteen month term that allows one rate increase; **36-Month Certificate**, the three year term; **60-Month Certificate**, the five year term.

## 4. What comes back

A single confirmation sentence in plain text. It repeats the certificate reference number, the official tier name the new term runs in, the first and last day of the new term as YYYY-MM-DD, the rate and the annual percentage yield as percentages with two decimals, and the count of terms the certificate has now run through as a whole number. Its arrival is what indicates the renewal was recorded; afterwards the certificate reads as active and pays the stated rate until the stated maturity date.
